keyVerseText: And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.
rootMeaning: The word ἀρχιποίμην (archipoímēn) combines two Greek roots: ἀρχή (archḗ), meaning beginning, chief, or ruler, and ποιμήν (poimḗn), meaning shepherd. This compound literally conveys the idea of the 'chief' or 'principal' shepherd, emphasizing not only guidance and care but also authority and leadership. Unlike the simple English term 'shepherd,' the root sense highlights a position of preeminence and governance over others.
usageInScripture: This term appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in 1 Peter 5:4, where it is translated as 'chief Shepherd.' Its rarity underscores its special significance, as it is used to describe Christ uniquely as the supreme shepherd over His flock. The consistent translation as 'chief Shepherd' reveals a focus on Christ's ultimate authority and care within the biblical text.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἀρχιποίμην as 'chief Shepherd' enriches our grasp of Christ's role as both leader and caretaker of His people. It affirms that Jesus is not merely one among many guides but holds the highest position of spiritual oversight and responsibility. This term encapsulates the intimate yet sovereign relationship between Christ and His followers, reminding believers that their ultimate hope and reward come under His wise and loving governance. It also points to the eschatological hope of His appearing, when His leadership will be fully revealed and rewarded.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Peter 5:4, the phrase 'when the chief Shepherd shall appear' points to the future return of Christ in His role as the supreme leader and caretaker of the church. The use of ἀρχιποίμην here emphasizes that this is not just any shepherd but the one with ultimate authority who will grant believers a crown of glory that never fades. This word highlights the certainty and honor of Christ's coming and the eternal reward He will bestow on His faithful followers.
